subject: Ownership playbook for route slices & cost delegation
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, sarah@cloudintegrations.io
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Ownership playbook for route slices & cost delegation

Team —

Quick ask: as we continue to roll out the per-route cost breakdowns for Console, product wants a short, concrete runbook that answers two questions: (1) who owns each "slice" (route, model variant, or tenant slice) for instrumentation and (2) how do we delegate cost/latency attribution (and handoffs) when an alert fires.

Context: Acme is piloting the per-customer route tiles and wants to know who to contact when the tile indicates a high-cost spike. We need something concise we can hand to SREs, CS and account teams.

Desired deliverables for next week:
- 1 page runbook (owners + escalation steps + sample Slack snippets)
- 2 quick win UI additions (owner badge on the slice tile, and a "create incident" quick action)
- list of sampling rates and the estimated cost impact (ballpark) for each tier

I've attached a draft of the ownership model and a spreadsheet with sample rates. Can you review and call out anything that will block the MVP?

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Product Manager, Observability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: slice-ownership-draft.pdf (3 pages), sample-rate-proposals.xlsx (sheet: assumptions)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, sarah@cloudintegrations.io
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Ownership playbook for route slices & cost delegation

Thanks Marissa — good framing. A few technical constraints to call out up front:

1) "Owner badge": we can surface an owner alias on the tile (name + team) easily. Persisting owner assignments will require a small API and DB table; estimate 1.5 engineer-days to wire up for the MVP and another day for permissions checks.

2) "Create incident" quick action: we can pre-fill an incident modal with the slice metadata and a generated query for the cost spike. That depends on the sampling window and whether we include full token traces. If we want token-level traces in the modal, that's another 2–3 days of work to ensure KV cache playback works in the background.

3) Sampling: the attached spreadsheet assumptions look reasonable. Note that sample rates below 1/100 will have noisy attribution. We should recommend a 1/20 baseline for tenant-critical slices during pilot.

Blocking items:
- Ownership lifecycle: who can change owner? product-only or infra?
- Slack/Incidents: do we want direct OpsGenie integration or just a deep link for now?

I can sketch a minimal API contract and a UI mock by Wednesday.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Staff Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Nice start — a couple UX notes from the console perspective:

- Owner badge placement: top-right of the tile works best; make it clickable and show contact card with rotation rules (primary, fallback).
- Quick action: instead of full incident creation, can we surface two choices: "Create incident" (OpGenie) and "Notify owner" (Slack DM template). The latter is lower friction for early pilots.
- Owner visibility: add an "owner history" tooltip so CS can see who owned this slice over the last 30 days (helps with noisy handoffs).

About the runbook: keep language short and prescriptive. Example steps:
1) On high-cost alert, run the provided cost-query with X window.
2) If owner responds within 15 mins, owner triages; otherwise escalate to SRE rotation.
3) Use the provided Slack template and add the incident link.

I'll update the draft and drop a lightweight mock in Drive by EOD Tuesday.

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Product Designer, Console
Redwood Inference
